name: shipment_tracking
description: Unattended batch check of many parcels: read a list of tracking numbers from a text file, look each one up against the carrier API, classify every parcel deterministically (delivered / out_for_delivery / in_transit / delayed / escalate / not_found / error), and write a single dated results file with a per-outcome summary. Never asks the user anything.

variables.description: Path to the plain-text file of tracking numbers, one per line. Default examples/shipment_tracking/tracking-ids.txt. To change the input file, edit this and the classify step's itemSource.file.
The list of decided records collected by the classify step, one per tracking number.

settings.action: For each tracking number in the input file, look up its live status with the carrier and decide an outcome. Do not invent statuses — use only the facts gathered per item.

itemVariables.description: True when the carrier lookup failed: a non-200 response, an empty body, a timeout, or a connection/exec error.
True when the carrier reports the tracking number is not found / invalid (HTTP 404).
The carrier status string, e.g. delivered, out for delivery, in transit, exception, returned, lost.
The carrier's estimated delivery date (YYYY-MM-DD), or empty.
Whole days from today until the estimated delivery date (0 when unknown).
True when the parcel is in transit AND its estimated delivery is more than the threshold (7) days away. Precomputed deterministically so the delayed branch is a simple boolean test.
True for delayed and escalate parcels (in transit and more than 7 days away, or exception/returned/lost).
Short human-readable summary of the parcel's facts.

conditions.condition: the tracking number was not found
the status is out for delivery

settings.action: Write the final batch report. Take the decided records in {results} (do NOT change any record's outcome) and write them as JSON to a file named tracking-status-<TODAY>.json, where <TODAY> is today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format. The JSON must be an object with: a `summary` field at the top holding `total` (the number of records) and `by_outcome` (a count of records grouped by their `outcome` value); followed by a `results` field holding the full list of decided records. Then the flow ends.
